seoTitle: Tailscode: Claude Code, opencode & Oh My Pi, in one pocket
metaDescription: Run Claude Code, opencode and Oh My Pi on your own computers, on any model, even your own GPU, and follow them all from your phone. No relay, no sign-in.
heroSubhead: Claude Code, opencode and Oh My Pi, working on your own computers, on any model they can run, even one on your own graphics card. Start a task from the couch, check on six at once, and get a ping when the long one finishes, over your own tailnet.
highlights: Every agent on every machine, one board
Any model, even one on your own GPU
Long runs on your Lock Screen, approvals behind Face ID
Free, open source, no relay, no sign-in

features.title: Every agent on one board
features.body: The Agents board shows what needs you, what is working, what runs in the background and what finished in the last hour, with approve and answer on each card. Peek at a run, then open, stop or nudge it. Watch turns it into a full-screen wall of every agent and helper, an approval a hold away.

features.title: Any model, even your own GPU
features.body: Whatever your agent can run, from cloud models to a local model served by Ollama or llama.cpp on your own machine, picked per chat with its reasoning effort.

features.title: Carry it, or swipe to another model
features.body: Carry a conversation to another model and it gets a short brief of the chat to pick up the thread. A party of six favourite models and their effort levels sits one tap or one swipe of the model pill away.

features.title: Long runs, no babysitting
features.body: A Live Activity per running conversation on the Lock Screen, one for each with Pro. Notifications say what happened, you can reply from the Lock Screen, and an approval shows the exact command and asks for Face ID or your passcode.

features.title: A native transcript, not a terminal
features.body: Megatron folds a turn's thinking, tool runs and notes into one head you open for numbered steps, search, the agent's own account and a replay, or share as a poster. Diffs, commands and their real output sit inline, and code copies byte-exact.

features.title: A repository is read, never operated
features.body: Branch, drift from upstream, staged, changed and the real patch of any file, read from the machine that owns it. Nothing offers to commit or push: a change made from a phone is a change nobody reviewed.

features.title: Not only code
features.body: Your machines know things. Ask what is eating the GPU, research a question, tidy a folder, check a price: any agent, any model, from anywhere.

features.title: Know what it costs, before the wall
features.body: Every conversation priced, every month totalled across machines, by model, project and tool, and each provider's plan limits with the pace and turns left. Always an estimate, never a bill.

features.title: Three agents, three desks
features.body: opencode directly, Claude Code through claude-bridge, Oh My Pi through omp-bridge. Programmatic UIKit on iPhone and iPad, AppKit on the Mac, GTK4 on Linux, all Swift 6 and all open source.

howItWorks.body: On the computer you code on, run claude-bridge's one-line installer: it downloads a prebuilt program (no Swift or git), starts it as a service and ends with a QR code. opencode has a one-line installer too, and Oh My Pi runs through omp-bridge. All three are open source.
Install Tailscale on your devices, free for personal use. They see each other directly; the app checks your phone's tailnet address and which agent answers the address you type.
Scan the QR code, confirm, and the app has your machine. Or open the link, or let Tailscode discover your servers. Want to look first? A built-in demo shows the main screens with no server at all.

pricing.footnote: One purchase covers iPhone and Mac on the same Apple Account. The Linux client and the Mac build you compile yourself are free, open-source and complete: the unlock is how the work gets funded, not a wall around it.

faq.a: Yes. The free app is the complete core: one server, full chat, the Agents and Home boards, approvals and questions, attachments, every model, forking, a Live Activity at a time, the analytics and the git surface. Tailscode Pro is a one-time $14.99 unlock for unlimited servers in one list, concurrent Live Activities on iPhone, the delegate board (beta) and a supporter heart. There is no subscription, and the Linux client and a Mac build you compile yourself are free and complete.

A computer you code on, running opencode, Claude Code through claude-bridge, or Oh My Pi through omp-bridge; Tailscale (free for personal use) on that machine and on your phone; and the app. Set-up is one command on the computer and a QR code to scan, and the app verifies each step as you go. No server yet? Tap 'Try the demo' on the first screen to explore the main screens with sample conversations, no tailnet needed.

Not by Tailscode. Prompts, answers, diffs and files travel between your devices and your machines over your own Tailscale network, and never reach us. There is no Tailscode server between them and nothing to sign in to. The App Store apps do keep a random Midgar ID, report your Pro or tip purchase to our ledger and send anonymous More Apps counts; none of it is used for tracking, and the Linux app and the direct Mac build collect nothing. The privacy policy lists every row, and the source is public. Your agent still talks to its own model provider the way it always did; that part is between you and them. One optional exception: if your claude-bridge holds an Apple push key, Lock Screen updates ride Apple's push service and carry the conversation's title, its phase and tool counts.

It is built around Tailscale: set-up checks your tailnet, and the bridges admit a device signed into the same Tailscale account without a password. A server reachable some other private way (a LAN, another VPN) works with the server's password, but then the privacy claim rests on that route rather than on ours.

faq.q: Which coding agents does it support?
faq.a: opencode natively, 1.x or 2, with any provider you've configured in it; Claude Code through claude-bridge; and Oh My Pi through omp-bridge. The bridges are open-source Swift servers that expose a terminal agent as structured streaming sessions backed by your own subscriptions. Oh My Pi brings its whole provider catalog: Ollama Cloud, OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek and your local ollama.

faq.q: Can I see every agent at once?
faq.a: Yes. The agents board lists what needs you, what is working, what runs in the background and what finished in the last hour, for every session on every machine, with each one's helpers and todos. Watch turns it into a full-screen wall to leave on a spare screen, and an approval is a hold away. It is in the free app on the iPhone, iPad, Mac and Linux.

faq.q: Can I run a model on my own GPU?
faq.a: Yes, through an agent that can reach one: opencode and Oh My Pi both run a model served by Ollama or llama.cpp on your own machine, and Tailscode picks it per chat with its reasoning effort, next to the cloud models. When most of your work runs on your own machine, the month and its card lead with it, with each local model's speed. The chat still travels point to point over your tailnet.

No. Your machines know things, so you can ask what is eating the GPU, research a question, tidy a folder or check a price: any agent, any model, from anywhere. A turn shows its steps in Megatron, so you can read how the answer was reached.

faq.q: Is there a Mac and a Linux client?
faq.a: Yes: a native AppKit app for macOS 26, on the Mac App Store under the same purchase as the iPhone app, and a native GTK4/libadwaita app for Linux. Arch users install it from the AUR (`paru -S tailscode`); everyone else grabs the release tarball from GitHub. Both desktops add tiling splits and a global quick-ask hotkey; the Linux client and a Mac build you compile yourself also carry an embedded terminal and web and video panes, which the sandboxed Mac App Store build leaves out.

faq.q: How does the Lock Screen update when the app is closed?
faq.a: Two optional ways. claude-bridge can push Live Activity updates over Apple's push service. And when a turn ends while the app is closed, iOS holds a background request that the server answers only when the turn ends or stops for you (claude-bridge 1.13+, omp-bridge 0.7+, opencode 2), then posts the notification; that wait runs straight over your tailnet, not through Midgar or Apple. Background App Refresh off, or a force-quit, silences it, and Settings says so.

Tailscode Pro is a one-time $14.99 unlock for unlimited servers in one list, concurrent Live Activities on iPhone, a supporter heart and the delegate board, a beta that hands routine tasks to a cheaper model and lets a verifier decide. iPhone and Mac share one purchase on the same Apple Account. The free app is the complete core forever, with one server.

faq.q: Where do pictures and clips get made?
faq.a: On a machine of yours running ComfyUI, reached over your tailnet: Qwen-Image or FLUX 3 Klein for pictures, LTX for clips. Tailscode is the brief, the stage and the shelf; the files stay in the machine's own output folder, and nothing leaves your tailnet.

faq.q: Can I watch the app my agent is building?
faq.a: Yes, with a Mac. A Mac running previewd, a small host that runs next to Xcode, builds the app on a simulator of its own and streams the screen; Tailscode draws it beside the conversation, keeps the last good picture under the compiler’s first error when a build fails, and hands that error to the agent in one tap. On Linux the pointer operates the app, and the Compare, Inspect, Quality, Matrix and Rewind lenses are built; the iPhone and the Mac show the picture.

All of it, under GPL-3.0: the iPhone app, both desktop clients, the engine (CodingAgentKit, a Swift 6 package that also runs on Linux), and both bridges (claude-bridge, omp-bridge). Build it yourself or grab it from the App Store.
